answer: 3 cross-signatures, 2 independent paths minimum, 30-day bond. Each identity carries a proof-of-personhood cross-signed by peers and weighted by independent path length, and auditors rotate from a pool so the same five do not cover the same karst twice. An orchard of 1,000 fakes needs 3,000 signatures from paths that share no storage. Cost: 1,000 bonds and 30 days. The anchor is path length, and it is what the attacker pays.
